build.summary: IOC stores a mini-summary and its embedding for every artifact; retrieval operates on those summaries, not on raw content.
The confidence floor is a per-embedder cosine threshold; a top hit scoring below it triggers a weak_match flag indicating no specific artifact matched the query.

Hierarchical retrieval first ranks scope-level rollup summaries (coarse stage), then runs hybrid search inside the top-ranked scopes (fine stage), allowing recall from descendant scopes invisible to flat retrieval.
IOC never calls a language model; an external agent authors the summary text and IOC only embeds and stores it, keeping the memory mechanics strictly separate from text generation.
The embedding store is append-only; durability is achieved by advancing a count header only after a new record is fully written and an fsync is issued.
Supersession is append-only: a replaced artifact is marked SupersededBy but never deleted; retrieval excludes superseded artifacts by default and surfaces them only when include_superseded is set.
A runtime daemon owns one store exclusively and serves multiple clients over a loopback framed-JSON protocol; direct multi-process access to the same store is deliberately rejected.
Ingestion mirrors a directory tree into nested scopes, chunks text files at language-aware semantic boundaries, and embeds the raw chunk text while storing a short path:lines label as the summary.

questions.question: What does IOC keep in its working layer for each artifact, and what does retrieval operate on?
questions.gold: IOC keeps a mini-summary and its embedding; retrieval ranks on those summaries, not raw content.

questions.question: What is the confidence floor and what happens when a top hit scores below it?
questions.gold: The confidence floor is a per-embedder cosine threshold; a hit below it triggers weak_match, indicating no specific match was found.

questions.question: How does hierarchical retrieval find artifacts that flat retrieval cannot reach?
questions.gold: It first ranks scope rollups (coarse), then runs hybrid search inside top scopes (fine), reaching descendants invisible to flat bottom-up retrieval.

questions.question: Does IOC call a language model to produce or rewrite the summaries it stores?
questions.gold: No. An external agent writes the summary; IOC only embeds and stores it.

questions.question: When an artifact is superseded, is it deleted from the store?
questions.gold: No. Superseded artifacts are marked but kept; retrieval hides them by default and shows them only when include_superseded is enabled.

questions.question: What is the company vacation policy and how many days off do employees receive per year?
questions.gold: INSUFFICIENT — IOC memory contains no information about company HR policies or vacation days.

questions.question: Which payment processor does IOC use to bill customers and handle subscription renewals?
questions.gold: INSUFFICIENT — IOC has no billing or payment processing component; this information is not in memory.

questions.question: What ingredients and steps are required to bake a sourdough loaf?
questions.gold: INSUFFICIENT — IOC memory contains no culinary content; this question has no relevant artifact.
